Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 2! The Australian players march out on the field and spread out to take their respective field positions. Kraigg Brathwaite walks out to bat in his landmark 100th Test, and his opening partner is John Campbell. Mitchell Starc will be bowling with the new ball. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Darren Ganga is pitchside. He mentions that the conditions are overcast and cloudy, and the pacers would love to operate at the start of the day. He believes there are very few indentations on short-of-good and good-length areas, meaning it shouldn’t be unplayable for the batters. He mentions that the degree of swing was 1.3 on Day 1, and that is something that will be there in the first 20-odd overs on Day 2 as well. He adds that there has been a lot of bounce in the surface compared to Barbados (20 cm additional bounce). He believes that WI batters should take a page from Carey and Webster’s batting yesterday, where they played defensively against good length and pounced on anything short or full.

Alzarri Joseph of the West Indies also shares a few words. On asked about his four-wicket haul, he says that the pitch had good assistance and that helped him, in addition to that, he tried to be consistent. He mentions that their Analyst has been doing a very good job of making good plans against the opposition batters. On Smith’s wicket, he says that Smith is someone who doesn’t shy away from attacking, and they had some plan in place, which eventually worked. On bowling out Aussies for 286, he says that it was a good effort and he feels the team could have been patient and got them bowled out a touch under 286. For what WI batters should look to do today, he says their batters should firstly assess the wicket and see the pace of the wicket, and then they should look to attack.

Alex Carey of Australia is up for a quick chat. He says that they got off to a decent start but lost a couple of wickets quickly. Adds that he and Webster could take their time out and play according to the situation and get through a tough period. Mentions that he does not think much about the scoreboard and tries to keep a positive mindset, and he is enjoying his batting at the moment. Praises Webster for the way he batted and says that he has stepped up for the team whenever needed and they can rely on him. Ends by saying that they showed good intent and are happy with the total, but they would have liked some more and hope that the bowlers can get a few quick wickets.

Not far away from the action now, the pitch is being rolled on and the groundstaff are working to prepare the outfield, as there was some overnight rain. However, no signs of any rain now, but the live visuals show that it is pretty overcast, and the Aussie seamers will be itching to go out and bowl in these conditions.

The weather at the stadium is expected to be cloudy, with some rain predicted later in the day. So overall, it will also be interesting to see if it has any impact on the pitch. Yesterday, we saw movement drying down a bit in the 2nd session, so from the West Indies' point of view, their first target will be to go to Lunch with minimal damage. The play will start in about 35 minutes from now, so stay tuned for the pitch report and further updates.

Now coming to today's action, West Indies batters will have their tasks cut out against the famed Aussie pace trio of Cummins, Hazlewood, and Starc. The wicket, as we talked about earlier, has aided pacers, and the Aussie pace trio will surely enjoy bowling on this surface. In fact, their fourth pacer, Beau Webster, can also be a handful with his medium pacers on this topsy-turvy wicket.

Well, coming to the wicket, on Day 1 it aided pacers from the word go, as there was consistent movement off the wicket and in the air throughout the day. In fact, there was variable bounce on display too, as there were quite a few deliveries that stayed low or bounced a touch extra. If Pat Cummins's dismissal yesterday is anything to go by, then this surface is only going to get tougher to bat on. The Windies pacers, led by Alzarri Joseph, did a fairly good job to reduce the Aussies to 110/5. But then it seemed like the pacers took the pedal off the accelerator in the 2nd session, as the last 5 wickets added 176 runs to the final total. Eventually, Alzarri Joseph finished with a four-fer. Jayden Seales got two, and the rest of the pacers took one apiece.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the 2nd Test between the West Indies and Australia. On Day 1, rain played a bit of a spoilsport, as we could get in only 66.5 overs yesterday, and that is the reason we will have an early start today. Though only 66.5 overs were possible on Day 1, it was not short of entertainment as we saw Australia getting bowled out for 286. For Australia, as many as 9 batters got into the double figures, but only Beau Webster and Alex Carey managed to cross the 30-run mark. The duo of Webster and Carey, in a way, not only saved the Aussie batting from a collapse but also managed to get a score that is perhaps a touch above par on this wicket.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

And that wraps up an eventful Day 1 of the 2nd Test! Despite a few rain interruptions, there was no shortage of action, with both sides battling it out fiercely. We’ve lost around 23 overs, so to make up for it, 98 overs are scheduled for Day 2. There will also be an early start, with play set to begin at 1.30 pm GMT. As always, we’ll be here with all the build-up, so don’t forget to join us. Until then, take care, and goodbye!

Beau Webster, one of the half-centurions for Australia, is up for a quick chat. He says that the ball did swing and seam, and in addition to that, he feels there was variable bounce as well, which made it tough, but he stuck to his game plan, and it helped. He is happy with the score, and he feels that it would have been great if he had batted a bit more with the tail and gone past 300. He hopes that the wicket will get tougher as the game progresses, and batting in the last innings will be a big challenge.

Australia carried their momentum into the final session, with Alex Carey reaching his fifty and the stand with Beau Webster crossing 100. Carey fell soon after, but Webster stood firm to notch up a gritty half-century. The lower order added useful runs before Greaves, Alzarri, and Seales struck in quick time, followed by a brief rain break. Post resumption, Webster tried to farm the strike but was run out for 60 after a misjudgment, as the tail dragged the total close to 300. West Indies openers would have thought that they had to face a couple of overs, but Bad Light ensured otherwise.

After a brief rain delay, Australia took control in the second session. Travis Head and Beau Webster pushed the total past 100 before Head fell to Shamar Joseph, thanks to a sharp catch by Hope. From there, Alex Carey and Beau Webster took charge, stitching together a fluent 99-run stand. While a few chances went begging, the duo batted with authority and kept the scoreboard ticking, putting the Windies under pressure.

Australia started steadily after opting to bat, with the openers showing positive intent, but a sudden collapse saw them slip from 47/0 to 50/3 in a span of three overs, with Alzarri Joseph striking twice and Anderson Phillip chipping in. Despite the wobble, Travis Head and Cameron Green counter-attacked to steady the innings, but just when things looked to be settling, Jayden Seales removed Green on the stroke of Lunch, denying him a chance to capitalise after being dropped.

A dramatic day of Test cricket comes to an unexpected end due to BAD LIGHT! Both teams had their share of moments, with West Indies impressing in the morning and evening sessions, but Australia’s positive approach and control during the afternoon, scoring at over four runs an over despite losing wickets, has given them a slight edge heading into Day 2.

We’re all set for West Indies’ reply as the players make their way out... but wait, there’s a twist! Just as they were heading to the middle, the umpires pulled out the light meter and weren’t satisfied with the reading. They have instructed the players to go off and call it a day. STUMPS ON DAY 1! The Windies openers will breathe a sigh of relief, avoiding a potentially tricky period, while Australia will be a touch frustrated, having hoped to snatch a breakthrough or two before close.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

West Indies might be slightly disappointed with their overall effort, knowing they let a few chances slip in the field, missing run-out opportunities, and dropping a couple of catches. Still, it was a fairly decent bowling performance. Alzarri Joseph led the attack brilliantly with a four-wicket haul, while Jayden Seales picked up a couple. Apart from Roston Chase, every other bowler contributed with a wicket. Now, the focus shifts to their batters, who have the task of negotiating a tricky spell before Stumps.

Australia have posted a strong total of 286 here, largely built on the backbone of another solid middle-order effort. Alex Carey and Beau Webster played pivotal roles, stitching together a vital 112-run partnership that pulled them out of trouble and shifted the momentum their way. While four of the top five got starts without pushing on, it was the middle and lower order once again that stepped up, with both Carey and Webster notching impressive fifties and the tail chipping in valuable runs to round off a well-rounded batting effort.

The old Dukes ball does start to reverse around the 50th over and with some dark clouds hovering around the stadium, the next session could be the right opportunity for the Windies to end the day on a high. As far as Aussies are concerned, well they will want the duo of Webster and Carey to extend this partnership further and end the day in a commanding position. So do join us for the post-Tea session in about 20 minutes time.

The movement from the wicket definitely dried down a touch, and the Dukes ball too became old in this session. But the major problem for WI was their inconsistent bowling in comparison with the first session, where they were bang on the target. Perhaps the counterattack of Carey took them by surprise, and from then on the momentum firmly shifted in favor of the Aussies. Carey was dropped by Shai Hope towards the fag end of the session, which summed an already miserable session for the hosts.

SESSION SUMMARY - 116 Runs, 25 Overs, 1 Wicket. A session thoroughly dominated by the Aussies. After Head's departure early in the session, the Aussies didn't look back as the duo of Webster and Carey stitched together an unbeaten partnership of 99, scoring at a rate of just over 4.5 an over. Such was the domination from both the batters in that session. Carey batted with a positive intent from the word go, as he didn't allow the WI pacers to settle on their lengths when bowling to him. On the other hand, Webster was slow to start, as at one point he was on 12(33), but then, as the session progressed, he found his touch on this wicket and changed gears.

Going into the second session, Australia would have their hopes tied down on Webster-Head to yet again rescue them from a tricky situation. On the other hand, WI pacers who have bowled with a lot of discipline in the first session will look to continue their good work. It will be interesting to see if the conditions do flatten out a bit in the next session. So do join us for the post-Lunch session at 4.43 PM GMT.

After that Green and Head came together and batted with good intent, as they kept the scoreboard ticking and put on a 43-run stand. Green looked at his best in that session and was also lucky to survive when John Campbell dropped a sitter at short covers. However, he didn't capitalize on it as he perished four balls later right on the cue of Lunch.  WI pacers, were on the money from ball one, as all the pacers, kept on beating the bat frequently. Alzarri Joseph started off poorly in his first over but was quick to get into the rhythm, as he picked up two wickets in his next two overs, which included the big wicket of Steven Smith.

SESSION SUMMARY - 93 runs and 4 wickets in 23 overs! End of the 1st session on Day 1, and this Test has kicked off in an entertaining fashion, as though four wickets fell in the session, batters scored their runs at just over four runs an over. There was consistent help for the pacers throughout the session, and the WI pacers didn’t disappoint as they were on the money with their lines and lengths. To start the session, Khawaja and Konstas scratched through the first 10 overs as they put on 47 for the first wicket. Particularly, Konstas demonstrated aggression right from the start. On the other hand, Khawaja looked tentative throughout his 29-ball stay at the crease as he eventually fell in the 11th over to an in-ducker from Alzarri, but not before completing 6000 Test runs. In the period from the 11th over to the 13th over, in total three wickets fell, as Konstas and Smith got out in consecutive overs after the fall of Khawaja.

We are moments away from the start of the action, but before that, players from both sides line up for the national anthems. It will be Grenada's first, followed by the national anthem of Australia, and it will conclude with the Rally 'Round the West Indies.

A proud moment for West Indies cricket as Kraigg Brathwaite will walk out for his 100th Test match, becoming only the 10th West Indian to reach this iconic milestone. A pillar at the top of the order, Brathwaite has been the face of resilience and grit in a challenging era for Caribbean cricket. From debuting as a teenager to leading the side with quiet determination, this landmark is a testament to his dedication, discipline, and unyielding love for the longest format.

PITCH REPORT - Darren Ganga is pitchside. He starts by saying that there hasn’t been any cricket at this venue for the last 12 months. He mentions that there’s an even covering of grass on this wicket as compared to Barbados, where there was patchy grass, which led to uneven bounce. He mentions that the surface at the river end looks more even, but from the Darbeau end, it doesn’t quite look even, which might present challenges to the batters. He mentions that there have been only 4 Tests played at this venue, and in those games, the 1st innings average score has been 278, whereas the 2nd innings score has been 80 runs more. He mentions that this pitch has traditionally offered something for the bowlers at the start.

Roston Chase, the skipper of West Indies, says that he has never played here, but the pitch looks decent, and they are happy to bowl first. Adds that they played good cricket for at least two innings in the last game but then let themselves down by leaking a lot of runs, which they have to work on. Mentions that he is very happy and proud of his friend, Kraigg Brathwaite, for playing his 100th Test and praises his longevity for the national side. Informs that they have made one change as Anderson Phillip comes in for Jomel Warrican, as the data shows this is a more seamer-friendly wicket.

Pat Cummins, the Australian Captain, says that he feels the wicket should play well for batting, but he isn’t one hundred percent sure about it. He mentions that very rarely a team plays a Test where all the batters do well, and he was pleased with how the middle order performed in the last game. On the return of Steve Smith, he says it’s a huge benefit, he has scored runs all over the world, and also adds that though he hasn’t played here, his presence will be of big help for their batting line up.
